method: Source-only review against inventory EXT-F-1003-T46 and forcing-function-tests; no test, browser, build or runtime mutation executed.

A_acceptance_evidence.verdict: NOT ACCEPTED; runtime pending and source cannot support attributable rediscovery
A_acceptance_evidence.requirement: inventory.json:3813-3848 requires valid save plus actual worker rediscovery, blank clear and invalid rejection. A healthy desktop connection or changed status label is not an explicit expected result, so replacing that old extra wording does not itself weaken T46.
A_acceptance_evidence.preserved: Trusted input, valid reload persistence, invalid retention, same-render invalid-to-blank, cleared reload persistence remain in source, but the undefined identifier prevents reaching the latter checks.

findings.title: Removed VALID_PORT still used in persistence assertion
findings.evidence: tests/browser/settings-local-controls-acceptance.mjs:252 references VALID_PORT twice after its declaration was removed at :15. After a successful probe and reload, evaluation throws ReferenceError and skips invalid-range and same-view blank checks.
findings.remedy: Use observedPort.port consistently; inspect remaining removed-name references before browser admission.

findings.title: Probe before next alarm is not attributable to Save rediscovery
findings.evidence: Runner :231-247 observes only method/path/time. bootstrap.ts:156-166 creates the alarm before asynchronous bootstrap probing, and :286-287 can already be executing an earlier alarm. bridge.ts:31-38 awaits native probing before discovery.ts:141-151 reads the latest override. Either independent probe can therefore reach the new port before nextAlarm even if the rediscover handler does no work. No worker lifetime, in-flight probe, handler invocation or request initiator is recorded.
findings.remedy: Keep rediscovery unverified until a read-only worker trace correlates the real Save message with its handler/probe, or establish and verify a boundary that excludes startup and in-flight probes. Prove a no-op rediscover handler cannot pass in an admitted isolated mutation run.

findings.title: HTTP observer marks working native rediscovery as failure
findings.evidence: bridge.ts:31-36 returns successfully for a healthy native host before any HTTP probe. The disposable browser profile does not remove machine native-host registration, and the runner establishes no native-unavailable precondition. Correct native rediscovery therefore times out waiting for GET /health.
findings.remedy: Observe actual handler completion independently of transport, or explicitly establish an HTTP-only test precondition and classify unavailable coverage honestly.

cleanup_and_timeouts: The listener returns 503 and is closed in outer finally after owned-browser disposal; no fabricated healthy response or worker mutation is introduced. Alarm wait is 35s and request wait 10s; >12s headroom is measured before trusted input, so slow actions can consume it and cause a false failure. Listener close has no separate deadline, though ordinary completed 503 requests and prior browser disposal make normal cleanup credible.
remaining: Repair runner identifier and attribution/transport evidence, then root-admitted browser execution, forcing-function negative proof and fresh evidence review. No runtime pass or product defect is claimed by this source review.
